title: guide a patient through a bounded healthcare conversation
input: The healthcare application starts an authorized conversation with approved clinical or administrative content.
action: Health Bot supplies the configured healthcare conversational experience and supported scenario logic. Its responses guide the defined workflow; clinical escalation and patient-data access follow the application's approved policy.
output: The application presents the appropriate guidance and hands off to a clinician or service team when required.
check: Review clinical content, escalation triggers, patient privacy and unsupported-query behavior before publishing the conversation.

title: verify a confidential runtime before releasing a protected key
input: The protected application submits supported platform attestation evidence to the configured verifier.
action: Azure Attestation evaluates supported evidence against the selected policy and returns an attestation result or token. The key service checks that result before release; an attestation token is not blanket authorization to all data.
output: The key-release component permits only the configured trusted workload to obtain the allowed key material.
check: Test expected measurements, invalid evidence, policy changes and token validation before allowing sensitive computation.

title: investigate a workload's cost increase and plan a validated change
input: The finance owner selects billing scope, tags, reporting window and budget ownership.
action: Cost Management presents supported cost analysis, budgets and recommendations using available billing data. Budget notifications signal thresholds; they do not automatically guarantee a hard spending cap.
output: The workload owner identifies the actual charge driver and proposes an approved capacity or retention change.
check: Check billing-data delay, allocation rules and actual resource effects before accepting savings estimates.

service: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management
title: assign a verified internet exposure to its owner
input: The security team configures approved discovery seeds and asset ownership review.
action: Defender EASM inventories supported external assets and exposure evidence. The security team validates the discovered relationship and prioritizes relevant issues; discovery does not grant authority to modify an unknown third-party asset.
output: The confirmed asset owner repairs the exposed configuration through its approved administration path.
check: Verify current external reachability, ownership and post-repair exposure before closing the finding.

title: provide an assigned development workstation with approved tooling
input: The developer requests a permitted workstation definition and project assignment.
action: Dev Box provisions the selected cloud development workstation under configured image, network and user policies. Development tools execute on the workstation; repositories and cloud resources retain their separate access controls.
output: The developer builds and tests the project while storing accepted code in the source repository.
check: Test image readiness, repository access, network restrictions and retention of uncommitted work before workstation replacement.

title: ingest governed subsurface data for an authorized energy analysis
input: The energy data owner supplies supported domain records, schemas and legal access metadata.
action: Energy Data Services supplies supported energy-domain data capabilities, including configured OSDU-compatible data workflows. Ingestion and entitlement settings determine available records; analytical applications perform their own geological calculations.
output: The authorized interpretation application queries accepted records and uses them in its domain analysis.
check: Validate schema, legal tags, entitlements and source-record reconciliation before sharing the dataset.

title: join an application VM to a managed domain
input: The identity owner selects the managed domain, synchronization scope and permitted VM network.
action: Domain Services provides supported managed domain capabilities such as domain join, LDAP or Kerberos under its configured directory and network settings. The application uses the appropriate domain protocol; identity lifecycle remains coordinated with Entra.
output: The application VM joins the domain and authenticates permitted corporate users or service accounts.
check: Test DNS, domain connectivity, password synchronization requirements and denied-user access before application rollout.

title: verify a supported credential before a business eligibility decision
input: The application requests a defined credential presentation with explicit user consent.
action: Verified ID supports configured verifiable credential issuance and presentation workflows. The verifier checks the accepted issuer and credential evidence; application policy determines whether the evidence satisfies the business requirement.
output: The application records only the needed verification result and applies its approved eligibility rule.
check: Test untrusted issuers, expired or invalid credentials, consent and minimum required claim retention.

title: develop and release an evaluated enterprise AI application
input: The team defines its AI task, permitted data, model choices and tool access.
action: Foundry provides the configured AI development and management environment for supported models, agents and tools. The application composes those deployed capabilities; project identity and policy govern permitted resources.
output: The team releases the accepted application after task-specific evaluation and records its model and tool configuration.
check: Test quality, source access, unsafe tool actions and rollback before opening the application to users.

title: export approved collaboration data for organizational analysis
input: The analyst requests the supported Microsoft 365 dataset with bounded tenant and user scope.
action: Graph Data Connect supplies approved bulk data access through its configured pipeline and consent process. Dataset availability and permission approvals determine what is exported; downstream analysis runs separately.
output: The analytics job computes permitted organizational aggregates from the accepted export.
check: Check consent, selected users, dataset completeness and output privacy before publishing analytical results.
